h1: Homebrewing in a small apartment: a small-batch setup that works
title: Homebrewing in a Small Apartment | Craft Beer School
desc: A small-batch homebrew set-up for a flat: equipment, space, smell, noise and cleaning, using brew in a bag and 5 litre batches.
teaser: No garage, no garden, a kitchen the size of a cupboard. You can still brew very good beer in 5 L batches.
standfirst: Brewing in a flat is mostly a question of scale. Brew in a bag, make 5 L at a time and you need one pot, one fermenter and a free shelf.
sections: A standard homebrew batch is 19 to 23 L (5 to 6 US gal). That needs a 30 L kettle, a fermenter you cannot lift easily and a lot of floor. A 5 L (about 1.3 US gal) batch fills about nine 500 ml bottles, fits in a stockpot and costs little if it goes wrong. It is also the best way to learn, because you can brew every week without building up a cellar of bad beer.

Use brew in a bag (BIAB). You need a pot of 10 to 12 L, a fine mesh bag that lines it, a kitchen scale, a thermometer and a long spoon. The grain sits in the bag in the water, the mash happens in the pot, then you lift the bag, let it drain and boil the wort in the same pot. There is no separate mash tun and no sparging equipment.

For a 5 L batch of beer around 5% ABV you need about 1.2 kg of malt and a pre-boil volume near 7 L. A glass or food-grade plastic jar of 6 to 8 L makes a fermenter with a lid and airlock. Add a hydrometer, sanitiser and a siphon with a bottling wand. The whole kit costs far less than a normal starter pack.

A domestic hob can boil 7 L without trouble. Induction is fastest and puts the least waste heat into the kitchen. Use the extractor fan and open a window, since a boil puts a litre of water into your air. Do not boil with a lid fully on, because DMS (a cooked sweetcorn smell) stays in the wort.

For chilling, stand the covered pot in a sink of cold water with ice added and swirl the water now and then. A 5 L pot cools to pitching temperature in 15 to 20 minutes this way and you need no chiller.

Mashing smells like warm porridge and the boil smells of wort and hops, which most people like and some do not. Brew when the building is awake. Dispose of spent grain the same day in sealed food waste, or compost it. A fermenter is silent apart from the airlock bubbling. Keep it in a wardrobe or a cupboard away from sunlight where the temperature is steady.

If you rent, check your lease for anything about gas or noise before you start and put a trivet under the hot pot so the worktop is not marked.
Fermenting and storing in tight spaces

One fermenter takes a wardrobe shelf. A stack of beer bottles takes a box under the bed. Keep the fermenter on a tray with a towel in case of overflow. Fermentation temperature is the real constraint in a flat: if the room is warm, see homebrewing in a hot climate.

Bottle in PET soda bottles if you worry about glass. PET lets you feel when the bottle is hard with carbonation and see how it is doing. Plan the carbonation carefully. Our guide on bottle conditioning in hot weather covers it.

You can take any recipe for 20 L and shrink it for the flat, but there are traps. Kettle losses do not scale and hop utilisation changes with the pot shape. Scaling a homebrew recipe explains how. Start with a pale ale, which you can make with simple ingredients, such as in brewing a clean pale ale in warm weather.

A small kitchen has nowhere to hide a mess. Clean as you go: rinse the pot while the sugars are fresh and wipe the worktop before the fermenter goes in. Keep the whole kit in one lidded box under a bed or on a high shelf, so the flat looks like a home again by evening.
A first batch you can brew this weekend

Mash 1.1 kg of pale malt and 0.1 kg of wheat malt in 8 L of water at 66 °C for 60 minutes. The grain soaks up about a litre, which leaves you near 7 L to boil. Lift the bag and drain it. Boil for 60 minutes with a small hop addition of about 5 g of a bittering hop at the start and 15 g of an aromatic hop at the end. Cool, pour into the jar, pitch a dry ale yeast and wait. Brewing every week lets you taste what changes and that is how a brewer learns.

If you enjoy it and want to understand why each step works, the next step is a structured course.
faqs: How much space do I need to homebrew in a flat?
A hob, a sink, a free shelf for the fermenter and a box for bottles. A 5 L batch needs one stockpot and one jar.
What is brew in a bag?
A method where the grain sits in a fine mesh bag inside the pot for the mash. You lift out the bag and boil the wort in the same pot.
Will homebrewing make my flat smell?
The mash and boil smell like porridge and hops for a couple of hours. Use the extractor fan and open a window.
Is it safe to bottle in a flat?
Yes if you prime carefully. PET bottles let you check pressure by feel and a closed box limits damage if one fails.
